clinicalPearls: Endometriosis is the presence of endometrial-like tissue outside the uterine cavity, most often on the ovaries, uterosacral ligaments, and pelvic peritoneum
Cardinal symptoms are cyclical and chronic pelvic pain, dysmenorrhoea, deep dyspareunia, and subfertility, though some women are asymptomatic
Symptom severity correlates poorly with the anatomical extent of disease
Ovarian endometriomas (chocolate cysts) contain altered, dark, degenerated blood
Definitive diagnosis has traditionally required laparoscopic visualisation, ideally with histological confirmation, though imaging can identify deep disease and endometriomas
Medical treatment suppresses cyclical ovarian activity to reduce pain, using hormonal therapies that induce a hypo-oestrogenic or progestogen-dominant state
Surgical management aims to excise or ablate deposits and restore anatomy, and can improve both pain and fertility
There is a recognised diagnostic delay of years, so a high index of suspicion in women with chronic cyclical pelvic pain is important
reference.pathophysiology: The most widely cited mechanism is retrograde menstruation, in which viable endometrial cells reflux through the fallopian tubes and implant on peritoneal surfaces. Additional contributions come from coelomic metaplasia, altered immune surveillance that fails to clear ectopic cells, lymphatic or vascular spread, and genetic predisposition. The ectopic tissue is oestrogen-dependent and responds to cyclical hormonal changes, causing local inflammation, repeated microhaemorrhage, fibrosis, adhesion formation, and distortion of pelvic anatomy. Chronic inflammation and nerve involvement generate pain and contribute to subfertility.
additionalDifferentials: Pelvic inflammatory disease and chronic pelvic infection
Irritable bowel syndrome and other gastrointestinal disorders
Interstitial cystitis or painful bladder syndrome
Ovarian cysts or masses of other aetiology
additionalInvestigations: Transvaginal ultrasound to detect endometriomas and signs of deep infiltrating disease
Pelvic MRI for mapping deep infiltrating endometriosis before surgery
Diagnostic laparoscopy with biopsy for definitive diagnosis and staging
Assessment of ovarian reserve and semen analysis when subfertility is a concern
Investigations to exclude bowel or bladder involvement when symptoms suggest it
redFlags: Cyclical bowel or bladder symptoms such as haematochezia or haematuria suggesting deep infiltrating disease
Ureteric involvement threatening silent renal obstruction and loss of kidney function
An enlarging or complex ovarian mass requiring exclusion of malignancy
Acute severe pain from a ruptured or torted endometrioma
Bowel obstruction from extensive adhesive or infiltrating disease
reference.prognosis: Endometriosis is a chronic, often relapsing condition. Pain and fertility frequently improve with medical or surgical treatment, but recurrence after stopping hormonal suppression or following surgery is common. Many affected women conceive spontaneously or with assisted reproduction, and symptoms typically regress after the menopause.
pitfalls: Dismissing severe dysmenorrhoea as normal and delaying diagnosis
Assuming minimal imaging findings exclude significant disease
Overlooking ureteric or bowel involvement in deep infiltrating disease
Relying on symptom severity to gauge disease extent
Neglecting the long-term and psychological impact and the need for a multidisciplinary approach
management: Start first-line analgesia with NSAIDs alongside hormonal suppression using combined hormonal contraceptives or progestogens to induce a progestogen-dominant, hypo-oestrogenic state and reduce pain
Escalate to second-line GnRH agonists or antagonists with hormonal add-back therapy to limit hypo-oestrogenic side effects
Offer the levonorgestrel intrauterine system as an effective progestogen-delivery option for pain and menstrual bleeding
Perform laparoscopic excision or ablation of endometriotic deposits with adhesiolysis when pain is not controlled medically or fertility is affected
For subfertility, refer to reproductive medicine for assisted reproduction rather than relying on hormonal suppression, which prevents conception
Refer deep infiltrating or bowel and bladder disease to a specialist endometriosis multidisciplinary team for excisional surgery
Provide long-term support for this chronic relapsing condition, addressing recurrence, chronic pain and psychological impact
